body: The builder of a planned 315-unit multifamily project in Riviera Beach sued the city's water utility district on Sept. 18, 2026, in Palm Beach County Circuit Court, the Palm Beach Post reported in an article republished by The Boca Raton Tribune. The plaintiff, 7920 Riviera Beach Holdings LLC, alleges the Riviera Beach Utility Special District is charging it new, much higher water and wastewater impact fees instead of the fees in effect when it submitted its plans.

The district's board approved the new fees on Feb. 19, 2025, raising the combined water and wastewater impact fee 157%, from $3,940 to $10,126 per unit, effective June 1, 2025. The lawsuit says the developer had submitted all permits for its project at 7880 N. Military Trail by April 24, 2025, and that the new fees would cost it $2.6 million and raise the project's cost by $1.6 million. It quotes a city official telling the developer that utility impact fees are set by the date of payment, not the date a permit number was issued. The developer says that position conflicts with the Florida Impact Fee Act, which provides that new or increased impact fees may not apply to permit applications submitted before the fee's effective date.

According to the suit, the district later issued revised invoices relabeling the fees as water and wastewater "capital charges," and its counsel asserted they are connection fees excluded from the Act; the district said it had "mistakenly used the word 'impact fee'" in its resolution. The Post reported that district documents, and the district's chief financial officer at the February 2025 meeting, described the charges as impact fees. The CFO said the increase was needed to help pay for a proposed water treatment plant estimated at $400 million, and the board imposed it immediately rather than phasing it in, citing extraordinary circumstances. Riviera Beach did not respond to the Post's request for comment.

timeline.label: Utility district board approves a combined 157% increase in water and wastewater impact fees
Developer has submitted all permits for its 315-unit project, according to the lawsuit
Developer sues the utility district in Palm Beach County Circuit Court
